chunks: A number of our companions narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman from Misma' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited hunting birds at night, and he said (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, the night is a sanctuary for them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hunting birds at night and the reasoning behind it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the prohibition of night hunting for birds, grounding the ruling in the concept of *aman* (safety/rest), which reflects the Shia emphasis on preserving the natural tranquility of creation. Scholars interpret this not merely as a practical restriction but as an ethical injunction against causing unnecessary distress to animals during their period of repose, aligning with the broader Islamic principle of *ihsan* (excellence) in treatment of animals.

en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Misma‘ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
prohibited hunting birds during the night, saying that the night is sanctuary for them.’”
